source.title: Rethinking the Rank Threshold for LoRA Fine-Tuning

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training-fit outcomes for LoRA fine-tuning of pretrained transformer encoders, a new setting for the claim's training-error behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training interpolation and a restricted-dimension training-fit result. Test-accuracy tables and rank comparisons are not training-error results. The cited results from Jang et al. and other prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures optimization of low-rank updates to pretrained transformers and synthetic matrix factorizations. None of the versions covers these systems: V1 specifies convolutional networks trained from random initialization, and V2 specifies two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks. Similar training-fit and landscape outcomes do not establish a test of either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the two training-fit observations but underrepresents the paper's main conclusion: rank one is competitive in the tested binary LoRA settings, whereas MNLI favors higher ranks. The theoretical MSE threshold relies on Gaussian-feature assumptions and an empirically calibrated constant; the CE result assumes PL and sufficient trainable dimension, and rank-one variance optimality assumes saturated bias. The experiments report no observed stalling, which does not establish the absence of all spurious minima.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains low-rank updates to pretrained transformer encoders with Adam and cross-entropy in a linearized NTK regime; it does not train full networks from random initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: Training fit changes when the NTK Jacobian is restricted to D = 32 effective dimensions; rank affects fit in that setting. The standard full-capacity setup interpolates at every tested rank.

fits_no_version.finding: All 140 canonical binary-task LoRA runs interpolated across seven ranks, four tasks and five seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linearized LoRA fine-tuning of pretrained RoBERTa-base can interpolate these few-shot binary datasets even at rank one.

fits_no_version.finding: With Jacobians projected to D = 32, training accuracy remained below 1 at every plotted rank, and higher rank improved training fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restricting effective feature dimensions can make LoRA rank a consequential capacity constraint on training fit.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix E reports synthetic rank-one matrix-factorization experiments whose spurious-stationary-point fraction falls below 5% at capacity ratios approaching 1.35 for larger target counts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested Gaussian-feature matrix-factorization setting, optimization success depends on the ratio of trainable manifold dimension to scalar targets.

record.problems: The models are pretrained encoders and only LoRA parameters are trained, so the results do not establish behavior from full-network random initialization. The projected-dimension result gives no exact training-accuracy values in the text. The theoretical CE result assumes the PL inequality.
record.rows_left_out: No additional training-fit outcomes stated beyond R1 and R2. Test-accuracy results were excluded because they do not measure training error.

untested.parts: All parts: randomly initialized convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including label corruption, model size, early stopping and regularization.
All parts: two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, joint teacher/student growth and adding one or two student neurons.
All parts: training degradation with depth, identity shortcuts and the stated initialization exceptions.
All parts: activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth.
All parts: learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature evolution and divergence.
All parts: batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. The projected-fit finding is explicitly supported by Figure 3's caption. Test accuracy and LoRA rank comparisons do not substitute for the behaviors and systems specified in V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Tests few-shot binary classification with pretrained encoders and LoRA in a linearized NTK regime. Does not test convolutional networks, CIFAR-10/100, random labels, full-network random initialization, smaller models, early stopping, or the listed regularized recipes.
No teacher-student two-layer ReLU width sweep or student-width comparison.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison or normalization ablation.
No initialization or depth sweep of the kind described.
No learning-rate stability-threshold or sharpness study.

rows.subject: RoBERTa-base
rows.size_stated: RoBERTa-base; layer-11 self-attention query and value matrices, m = n = 768
rows.stage_stated: pretrained model; LoRA training in the linearized regime
rows.operation_detail: Adam training of single-layer LoRA across ranks on four few-shot binary tasks; authors report aggregate interpolation across the runs.
rows.value: All 7 × 5 × 4 = 140 training runs converge to interpolation; no instance of stalling at a non-global stationary point.
rows.note: Aggregate statement over all ranks, seeds, and four tasks; the encoder is pretrained and the trained parameters are LoRA updates.
rows.check: The reported interpolation of all 140 runs is accurately extracted, but it concerns linearized LoRA fine-tuning of pretrained RoBERTa, outside V1's system and initialization conditions. Successful runs establish no observed stalling, rather than proving the landscape contains no spurious minima.

rows.subject: RoBERTa-base
rows.size_stated: RoBERTa-base; NTK Jacobians projected to D = 32 effective dimensions
rows.stage_stated: pretrained model; LoRA training in the linearized regime
rows.operation_detail: Trained LoRA after random orthogonal projections reduced the effective NTK Jacobian dimensions.
rows.value: figure only; text states training accuracy is below 1 for every rank.
rows.note: The text explicitly says training accuracy does not saturate at 1 for any rank; exact per-rank values are only in the figure.
rows.check: Figure 3's caption explicitly reports training accuracy below 1 at every rank, but exact accuracies are unavailable in the supplied text. This projected LoRA capacity experiment does not measure V1; below-perfect accuracy alone also cannot establish substantial error or exclude near-zero error.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
